To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the bremsstrahlungspectrum is the sum of the DRR and the bremsstrahlung tip, (2) the DRR and the tip have the same angular distributions, but the DRR has no polarization correlations, and (3) the tip angular distribution can be calculated from the DRR angular distribution using the method developed in the present paper.
(1) the angular distribution for the DRR process is not a dipole one and (2) the angular distribution and the polarization correlation for the bremsstrahlung tip are not dipole ones either.

(1) there is a connection between the brems-strahlung tip and the photoeffect; (2) the connection is a general one; (3) it is valid in the relativistic regime; and (4) it is not limited to the dipole approximation
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for calculating the angular distributions and polarization properties of the radiation emitted in the inelastic scattering of electrons and positrons from atomic targets.

the development of methods for the calculation of the cross sections of bremsstrahlung and of direct radiative re-combination, and with the comparison of the results with the results obtained by other methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the connection between the brems-strahlung tip and DRR is a good one.
the connection between the bremsstra-hlung tip and DRR is not perfect, but that it works very well in most cases, and that the agreement between theory and experiment is generally satisfactory.
the connection between the bremsstralung tip and the photoeffect is not perfect, but that it is sufficiently good for many purposes.

the nonrelativistically derived dipole approximation is inadequate for the evaluation of angular distributions and polarization-correlation coefficients for bremsstrahlungs and DRR processes, even for the lowest-energy transitions.

the bremsstrahlung tip and direct-radiatoradiative-recombination cross sections and angular distributions are closely related, and that the connection between them may provide a means of obtaining results for the bremsstraulung tip from corresponding results for the photoeffect.
